$comment: qops hooks. Wired per CADR-0001, which measured every event below. Commands invoke `qops <verb>` and nothing else; every project specific lives in .qops/config.yml. Invoked as `python -m qops` because a bare `qops` resolves in neither cmd.exe nor git-bash without a PATH edit, and a PATH edit is a machine fact that does not belong in a committed file.

permissions.$comment: Sign-off item 10, 2026-08-16. The rule the owner gave: if a prompt class has never once been answered no, it is allowlisted. That is four classes and no more - waits, reads, test runs, and `gh api` GETs. Everything here is machine-independent; absolute-path variants are a machine fact and live in settings.local.json. `gh api` bare is a GET, and the allow rule below covers only that. A write to repo settings, branch protection or a label set is still the owner's call every time - CADR-0003/CADR-0006 rest on those settings being what the owner last set them to - but the control for it is no longer six deny entries here. It is the guard (#235): a `gh api` call carrying a write method is refused in an unattended run, and in an attended one it reaches this harness's own permission prompt. A deny is absolute, so it never fell through to a prompt, and the owner entitled to make the call had no button.
